### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/spec`, touching **40** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **14** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/api.json`, `packages/spec/api-surface/system.json`, `packages/spec/authorable-defaults/system.json`, …), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**7** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/api/client-sdk.mdx`  _(via RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED (literal, a string literal in rateLimitError))_
- `content/docs/api/error-catalog.mdx`  _(via QUOTA_EXCEEDED (literal, a string literal in quotaError), RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED (literal, a string literal in rateLimitError))_
- `content/docs/api/error-handling-client.mdx`  _(via RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED (literal, a string literal in rateLimitError))_
- `content/docs/api/wire-format.mdx`  _(via RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED (literal, a string literal in rateLimitError))_
- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/error-handling.mdx`  _(via QUOTA_EXCEEDED (literal, a string literal in quotaError), RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED (literal, a string literal in rateLimitError))_
- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/http-protocol.mdx`  _(via RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED (literal, a string literal in rateLimitError))_
- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/realtime-protocol.mdx`  _(via RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED (literal, a string literal in rateLimitError))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **14** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/api.json`, `packages/spec/api-surface/system.json`, `packages/spec/authorable-defaults/system.json`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- the SDK route bridge reached **61** of **219** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **158** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **158**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **103** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **168** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 74fd4bf64abfd77fa611425b029aa26afcd6808a` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `2c9eb6a1e5088bf0ac0f9bf6790d9a75aeaa34a7` — the merge of head `88fe2df6c30c8ce034b16617a7495cc6bb666b71` into base `74fd4bf64abfd77fa611425b029aa26afcd6808a`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 2c9eb6a1e5088bf0ac0f9bf6790d9a75aeaa34a7 && git checkout 2c9eb6a1e5088bf0ac0f9bf6790d9a75aeaa34a7
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 74fd4bf64abfd77fa611425b029aa26afcd6808a 88fe2df6c30c8ce034b16617a7495cc6bb666b71 && git checkout -B drift-repro 74fd4bf64abfd77fa611425b029aa26afcd6808a && git merge --no-ff 88fe2df6c30c8ce034b16617a7495cc6bb666b71

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 74fd4bf64abfd77fa611425b029aa26afcd6808a
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 74fd4bf64abfd77fa611425b029aa26afcd6808a` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `88fe2df6c30c8ce034b16617a7495cc6bb666b71`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/api/index.ts, packages/spec/src/api/push-relay.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/system/push-config.zod.ts + packages/spec/src/api/errors.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/api/push-delivery.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/system/push-device.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/shared/refinement-projection.ts, packages/spec/src/shared/strict-object.ts, packages/spec/src/shared/lazy-schema.ts, packages/spec/src/system/push-config.zod.ts on `main` (read, not reviewed: the two new test files, `type-alias-convention.pin.test.ts`, the changeset, `variant-docs.json`, the regenerated `content/docs/references/**` and `packages/spec/{api-surface,authorable-*,declaration-map,export-origins,json-schema.manifest}/**`). The rest of the diff is the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`.

### ① Derived judgments

Accept-set of `PushServiceConfigSchema` (system), judged against `main`'s `{ apns?, fcm? }` strict block and the card's ask 1:

- `{}` parses to `{ transport: 'relay' }` — **right**: the card rules the relay the default. On `main` it parsed as "no vendor delivers"; nothing reads the shape (`[PLANNED — not yet read]` kept on all five schemas) and no stack key or door reaches `PushServiceConfigSchema` anywhere under `packages/` at this head (grep: only the spec module itself), so no deployment moves.
- `{ apns }`, `{ fcm }`, `{ apns, fcm }` with no `transport` parse as direct with `transport: 'direct'` filled in — **right**: the pre-relay shape keeps parsing, which is the widening the declaration claims. The mechanism holds on the code: both members default their `transport` literal, so `input.transport` absent is not in the discriminator map and `unionFallback: true` tries relay then direct; the relay strict block refuses the vendor key, the direct block accepts it.
- `{ transport: 'relay', apns | fcm | credentialRef | credential | token | apiKey | key | secret }` refused by name with the relay guidance pointing at `transport: 'direct'` — **right** (card: "credentials inside a relay block"). Strictness refuses every unknown key; the guidance rows only add the prescription, and the dev's ablation leg B measured that.
- `{ transport: 'direct' }` with no vendor block refused with one `custom` issue at `[]` — **right** (card: "direct without any credentialRef"). The rule is the projectable `requiredOneOf(['apns', 'fcm'])`, so the published JSON Schema carries it as `anyOf` of `required` and the dropped-refinements ledger does not move (it is not in the diff). A vendor block without its `credentialRef` is still refused at `['apns', 'credentialRef']`, as on `main`.
- `{ transport: 'direct', endpoint }` refused by name pointing at the relay — **right**, not asked by the card but the symmetric half of the mixed-shape rule.
- `{ transport: 'relay', endpoint: 'http://…' }` refused at `['endpoint']` — **right**: every request carries the binding bearer. No production URL is written into the spec; "absent means the production relay" is the describe text. The card said `endpoint` "defaults to the production relay"; declaring absence rather than a URL is the right reading, since the address is the cloud's to publish.
- `{ transport: 'hms' }` answers `invalid_union` — **right**; the card keeps `PushVendorSchema` at `apns | fcm` this phase, and it is unchanged.
- The one value `main` accepts and this head refuses is JavaScript-only: `{ apns: undefined }` with no vendor block (the strict relay block sees a present key, the direct block finds no vendor). No JSON document moves. Named by the dev in the PR body and the report; judged under ② below.
- Published JSON Schema: the union projects to one schema per member; `{}` satisfies the relay member only (direct fails its `anyOf` `required`), `{ apns }` the direct member only (relay has `additionalProperties: false`). So the published file and the runtime agree on every JSON document, with or without `oneOf` exclusivity.

Accept-set of the new `api/push-relay.zod.ts`, judged against the card's ask 2 and ruling 2A:

- Request `{ deliveries: [{ token, vendor, payload, priority }] }`, strict, `min(1)`, no credential in the body — **right**. `vendor` is the existing `PushVendorSchema`; `priority` is `high | normal` with the APNs 10/5 and FCM high/normal mapping in the describe text.
- Payload `{ data: PushDeliveryDataSchema, text }`, strict, with `title`, `body`, `subtitle`, `message`, `content` refused by name — **right** at the payload level (see ④ for the `data` level).
- Response `{ results: [{ token, status: ok | invalid | retry }] }` in request order — **right**; `invalid` is tied to the `UserDeviceSchema` row semantics (`enabled: false` plus `invalidatedAt`), which exist on `main` as cited.
- Error envelope: the house `ErrorResponseSchema` with `error` narrowed to a `code` union of three `EnhancedApiErrorSchema.extend(...)` members, `UNAUTHENTICATED` 401 with `details.reason` `binding_invalid | binding_revoked`, `RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` 429 with required `retryAfterSeconds`, `QUOTA_EXCEEDED` 429 with it optional, `helpText` required on all three — **right** against the card ("401 bad or revoked binding, 429 quota or rate limit with reason and next step"); all three codes exist in `StandardErrorCode` on `main`, so no ledger row is owed. `extend` on the `lazySchema` facade is the first such use in `src/`, and the facade forwards it (the tests parse through it and `Type Check · source gates` is green).

Public-surface changes: `api/index.ts` adds one `export *`; nine relay schemas with their input types and two `...Parsed` types; two transport members with input and `...Parsed` types plus `PushServiceConfigParsed` (ADR-0122, since parsing fills `transport` in). The pin file moves 822 to 828 (the union loses its isomorphic pin, seven relay schemas gain one; the two enums `PushRelayPrioritySchema` and `PushRelayResultStatusSchema` carry no `[PLANNED]` marker, which follows `PushVendorSchema` on `main`). Generated artifacts: `authorable-surface/system.json` moves `PushServiceConfig:apns|fcm` to `PushDirectTransportConfig:apns|fcm` and adds `transport` and `endpoint` rows; `authorable-defaults/system.json` gains both `transport` defaults; `json-schema.manifest` gains eleven defs; `variant-docs.json` exempts the error union as wire protocol (not-authorable), which is the right row for a shape nobody authors; `llms.txt` counts 34 to 35 api modules. All consistent with the source.

Gate families on this head (the check-runs are the verdicts): concluded **success** — Check Changeset, Check PR Size, PR-body guards, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Spec property liveness, Lint · ESLint, Lint · docs & code guards, Lint · repo & tooling gates, Lint · scoped (slot lookup & corpus, query-options erasure, tooling self-tests), Lint · PM dispatch-gates, Type Check · source gates, Build Docs, Build UI Deps, Dogfood Regression Gate, Check Documentation Links, Flag docs, Plan Test Core shards, filter, Auto Label. Skipped (opt-in or matrix placeholders): Packed-tarball smoke, 18.x harness, Temporal Conformance, UI Published Artifacts, Dogfood Verify CLI, Lint UI, Schedule gate. **Still pending at review time**: Build Core, Test Core 1-8, Test UI 1-16, Type Check · workspace, consumer gates, debt ledger and UI, Lint · CI release & engine gates, Lint & Repo Gates (queued), Build & E2E UI, Live E2E UI. The families judged here are the ones that concluded; the seat adopting this record confirms the pending ones are green before landing.

### ② Semver level

- `.changeset/29816-push-relay-transport.md`: `@objectstack/spec: minor` — **right**. The diff publishes new exports and new authorable keys from `@objectstack/spec`; nothing an author could write before is removed or tombstoned.
- `Clause-②: yes (widening)` on the PR body and the changeset — **right**. In the JSON domain every document `main` accepts (`{}`, `{ apns }`, `{ fcm }`, `{ apns, fcm }`) this head accepts, and the published JSON Schema is a superset of the old one. The JS-only `{ apns: undefined }` residue is a property of strictness meeting a present-but-undefined key and reaches no JSON author, no serialized config and no reader; a narrowing arm for it would declare BREAKING on a shape nothing reads, and the alternative (phantom `apns`/`fcm` undefined-only keys on the relay block) would put dead keys on the authorable surface. Answered under ③, open question 1: option A.
- `Metadata-protocol: added` — **accepted**. The authorable-surface baseline moves by added rows (`transport`, `endpoint`, the relocated vendor rows) and the gate reads `added` from them (Check Changeset green). The `semantic` arm ("a changed meaning or default") was weighed: `{}` reads as the relay here where `main`'s docblock read it as no vendor, but `PushServiceConfigSchema` is reachable from no metadata root at this head, so there is no authored `{}` whose meaning moves; the door that first makes it authorable is the change that owes the semantic reading if it keeps this default. Answered under ③, open question 2: option A.

### ③ Boundary flags

Open questions (os-dev-report 2026-11-03T09:37Z):

1. Keep `yes (widening)` despite the JS-only `{ apns: undefined }` refusal? **A — keep widening**, with the residue named in the PR body as it is. Reasoning in ②.
2. `{}` changes its declared meaning; `added` or `semantic`? **A — added**. Reasoning in ②. The first reader/door PR (#29794 for #29041) carries the declaration for the meaning it makes real.

Deviations (three): the attribution link pointing at the card thread — accepted, provenance only; "cloud ADR-0008" in place of the card's "ADR-0008" — **right**, this repository's ADR-0008 is the metadata repository and change log and the code says `cloud ADR-0008` as `packages/cloud-connection` does; no assignee, reviewer or activity subscription — accepted per the order.

Out-of-scope findings (two): which credential a cloud-hosted server (OS_CLOUD_API_KEY, no `oscc_` bearer) presents to the relay is the relay's to state — agreed, carrier cloud, and this spec says only that the binding credential is the bearer; #29794 reads top-level `apns`/`fcm` and owes the `transport` narrowing in service-push when it merges after this card — agreed with the seat's serial ruling, and it also owes taking the marker off the direct member only.

Premise: the order's "no open PR edits push-config.zod.ts" was false (#29794); the seat ruled this card lands first. Not escalated: the ruling is on the card thread and this head does not touch service-push.

No `security_findings`. The relay carries no credential in any schema; the `endpoint` is https-only; the payload refuses content by name at its own level.

### ④ Design judgment

**`packages/spec/src/system/push-config.zod.ts`** — judged against the card (ruling cloud#3519, 1C 2A 3A 4B 5A 6B 7B), `main`'s shape, and its first consumer (#29794's reader, held behind this card). **Holds.** Attempts to break it: a present-but-undefined `transport` with a vendor block (`{ transport: undefined, fcm }`) — the discriminator is a declared key on both members so it is not an unrecognized key, the default fills it, relay refuses `fcm`, direct accepts; `{ endpoint, fcm }` with no transport — both members refuse and zod answers `invalid_union` with both members' issues, which the PR body names and the house formatter picks a branch for; `apns: null` on direct — refused at `['apns']` by the vendor schema, and `requiredOneOf` plus JSON Schema `required` both count `null` as present, so runtime and published file agree; the relay's `.refine` ordering — zod runs the `custom` check only when the base object has no issues, so the dev's "exactly one issue" tests describe the real behaviour. The docblock's three claims (relay default, direct for white-label, the no-`transport` reading) match the code, and the "hosted surface out of scope" sentence is gone as the card asked. No finding.

**`packages/spec/src/api/push-relay.zod.ts`** — judged against ruling 2A (ID-only), the house error envelope in `api/errors.zod.ts`, `PushDeliveryDataSchema` and `UserDeviceSchema`, and its two consumers (the push channel #29041 and the cloud relay). **Holds, with two should-fixes:**

- **should-fix** — the ID-only rule is enforced one level deep. `PushRelayPayloadSchema` is strict and refuses `title`, `body`, `subtitle`, `message`, `content` by name, but `data` is judged by `PushDeliveryDataSchema`, a plain `z.object` on `main` that strips unknown keys. So `payload.data.title` is neither refused nor named: a parse strips it silently, while the describe text says the relay "puts it in the vendor message unchanged". A relay that forwards the raw body carries such a key to the device; one that forwards the parsed output drops it. Pick one and say it: either judge `data` strictly at the relay payload (a strict wrapper over the three `PushDeliveryData` keys, with the same content guidance), or state in `PushRelayPayloadSchema`'s describe text that the relay forwards the parsed `data`, never the raw body. Not a must-fix: the only party that could put content under `data` is the operator's own sender, and the ruling protects the operator from the relay, not the relay from the operator.
- **should-fix** — the 429 pacing member contradicts the house envelope's own example. `RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` requires `retryAfterSeconds` and says "the delivery may be sent again", but inherits `retryable: z.boolean().default(false)` from `EnhancedApiErrorSchema`, so a relay answer written without `retryable` parses to `{ retryable: false, retryAfterSeconds: 30 }`; the house `@example Rate Limit Error` in `errors.zod.ts` carries `retryable: true` and `retryStrategy: 'retry_after'`. The test passes `retryable: true` explicitly, so nothing pins the default. Fix `retryable` on the pacing member to `z.literal(true).default(true)` (and consider the same on `QUOTA_EXCEEDED` when `retryAfterSeconds` is present, or pin `category: 'rate_limit'`); both are `Parsed`-typed already, so no pin moves.

Also read and found sound: the response keyed by `token` is disambiguated by request order when one token appears twice in a batch (two notifications to one device), and the describe text says so; `PushRelayResultSchema` and `PushRelayResponseSchema` are intentionally non-strict (the relay may grow its answer), while the request is strict (the relay pins what it accepts), which is the right asymmetry for a wire the sender does not control; the cross-domain import of `PushVendorSchema` from `system/` follows `push-delivery.zod.ts` importing `system/push-server-origin`. No batch-size ceiling is declared on `deliveries`; that is the relay's pacing rule and belongs with its 429, not here.

**`packages/spec/src/api/index.ts`** — one `export *`, placed beside `push-delivery.zod`; `api-surface/api.json`, `export-origins/api.json` and `declaration-map/api.json` carry the nine schemas. **Holds.** No finding.

No must-fix. Both should-fixes are on the relay wire shape, which no producer or consumer serves yet (`[PLANNED — not yet served]`), so they can land in the follow-up that first serves it or in this PR at the seat's call.

**VERDICT: PASS**

- **Shape:** `PushServiceConfigSchema` becomes a `transport` union, the hosted relay (`{ transport: 'relay', endpoint? }`, no credential) by default and `{ transport: 'direct', apns?, fcm? }` for white-label builds; a body without `transport` keeps parsing (vendor blocks read as direct, `{}` as relay); credentials in a relay block and a direct block without `credentialRef` are refused at authoring. - **Gates:** every check-run on the head complete and green.
- **Landing:** not governed, 1393 changed lines. Ready + auto-merge now.
